items.definition:
unable to be taken away from or given away by the possessor
All people are born with certain inalienable rights.

not in harmony or keeping with the surroundings or other aspects of something
The modern sculpture looked incongruous in the ancient garden.

within the skull
The patient suffered an intracranial hemorrhage.

unable to be reduced or simplified
The problem was irreducible to a simple solution.

relating to or situated on the shore of the sea or a lake
The littoral zone is rich in marine biodiversity.

relating to the macula of the eye
Macular degeneration is a common cause of vision loss.

disastrous or destructive
The economic policies proved ruinous for the country.

acting as a cause
The causative factor for the disease was identified.

relating to or affected by congestion
He was diagnosed with congestive heart failure.

in low spirits from loss of hope or courage
After losing the game, the team was completely despondent.

occurring outside marriage
The scandal involved an extramarital affair.

happening by accident or chance rather than design; happening by a lucky chance
It was a fortuitous coincidence that they met at the airport.

fast and energetic in a rather wild and uncontrolled way
The frenetic pace of the city can be overwhelming.

arrogantly superior and disdainful
Her haughty attitude made her unpopular.

poor; needy
The city provides services for its indigent population.

within an institution or organization
They participate in intramural sports at the university.

impossible to reconcile; incompatible
They had irreconcilable differences that led to their divorce.

having, showing, or done with good judgment or sense
It was a judicious decision to invest in renewable energy.

deserving praise and commendation
Her efforts to help the community were truly laudable.

relating to logarithms
The data was plotted on a logarithmic scale.

Relating to or causing progressive damage to the nervous system
Alzheimer's disease is a common neurodegenerative disorder.

Relating to the back of the head or skull
The injury affected the occipital lobe of the brain.

Relating to the eye and its diseases
She visited an ophthalmic surgeon for her eye condition.

Characterized by vulgar or pretentious display; designed to impress or attract notice
He made an ostentatious display of his new wealth.

Relating to a system of medicine emphasizing the interrelationship of the body's systems and the importance of structural integrity
She sought treatment from an osteopathic physician for her back pain.

relating to the Pope; characterized by an air of superior knowledge or authority.
He delivered his speech with a pontifical air, as if he knew everything.

relating to the period after the end of colonial rule.
Many postcolonial nations faced challenges in establishing their new identities.

lying stretched out on the ground with one's face downward; completely overcome and helpless.
He fell prostrate before the king.

relating to or characterized by representation, especially of the external world in art or philosophy.
The artist moved from abstract to a more representational style.

working together to produce an effect greater than the sum of their individual effects
The team's efforts were synergistic, leading to a breakthrough.

relating to or characteristic of Tantra
She was studying tantric yoga practices.

not permanent or lasting
Life is full of transitory moments.

involving or guilty of treason
His actions were deemed treasonous by the court.

failing to produce the intended result
The coup attempt was abortive and quickly suppressed.

relating to the bottom of a sea or lake
Benthic organisms live on or in the seabed.

relating to or denoting a violent natural event
The eruption of the volcano was a truly cataclysmic event.

Oppressed or treated badly by people in power.
He fought for the rights of the downtrodden.

so good or unusual as to be impossible to copy; unique
Her inimitable style made her stand out from the crowd.

reluctant; unwilling
She was loath to admit her mistake.

Relating to or denoting the transformation of a rock or mineral by heat, pressure, or other natural agencies.
Metamorphic rocks are formed from existing rocks by heat and pressure.

Relating to both nerves and muscles.
Neuromuscular disorders affect the communication between the brain and muscles.

Relating to the penis.
The doctor examined the penile area.

Shining brilliantly; splendid or dazzling in appearance.
The queen looked resplendent in her coronation robes.

sparing in the use of words; abrupt.
He gave a terse reply, indicating his annoyance.

disloyal; betraying one's country or cause.
His actions were considered traitorous by many.

Relating to the Turkic peoples or languages.
Many Central Asian languages are Turkic.

Not mixed or diluted with any different or extra elements; pure.
The film was an unadulterated disaster.

Not proper or appropriate.
His behavior at the funeral was unseemly.

Not giving way to pressure; firm and resolute.
He faced the challenge with unyielding determination.

of doubtful authenticity, although widely circulated as being true
The story about the hidden treasure is probably apocryphal.

relating to or resulting from living organisms
The ecosystem is influenced by both biotic and abiotic factors.

relating to combinations
The problem required a combinatorial approach.

forming a part of something's essential nature
These principles are constitutive of our legal system.

relating to the crown of the head or a specific anatomical plane
The coronal suture connects the frontal and parietal bones.

enormous, gigantic
They faced a gargantuan task to clean up the entire park.

divine, resembling a god
The artist's skill was almost godlike in its perfection.

relating to the description of bodies of water
The hydrographic survey mapped the ocean floor.

arrogant, domineering
His imperious tone left no room for argument.

excessive; unusually large
He spends an inordinate amount of time on his hobbies.

on or toward the side sheltered from the wind
We sailed to the leeward side of the island to escape the strong winds.

full of lust; showing strong sexual desire
His lustful gaze made her uncomfortable.

having a gentle sheen or soft glow
Her long, lustrous hair cascaded down her back.

visible to the naked eye; not microscopic
The macroscopic features of the rock were clearly visible.

Excessively concerned with minor details or rules
His pedantic approach to grammar made the lesson tedious.
